title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: page 51 of the notes (archive p.103), in the section building the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} through their boundary strata, which are indexed by stable ('MD') dual graphs G. The previous page showed that the maps of fundamental groupoids induced by an arbitrary 'modulation' morphism reduce, via the normalisation of the stratum M_G (whose π1 is ∏_{α∈S(G)} π1 M_{g_α, Î_α}, with Î_α the half-edges and marked points at vertex α), to the maps (148) π1 M_{g,I} → π1 M_{g,I'} for I' ⊂ I. In modern terms these are the point-forgetting maps M_{g,I} → M_{g,I'}, which on π1 are Birman-type forgetful homomorphisms of mapping class groups / Teichmüller groupoids.

This page first remarks that, to describe these 'normalisation' morphisms together with their compatibility with isomorphisms (relabellings of I), one must use the condition attached to (148). The displayed formula 𝔖_{I,I'} ≃ 𝔖_{I'} × 𝔖_{I∖I'} most plausibly says that the stabiliser of I' in the symmetric group of I is the product of the two symmetric groups. The forgetful map is equivariant only for that stabiliser.

It then states a 'Programme', with a margin note: by generators and relations, in purely algebraic terms.
(i) Determine, up to canonical equivalence, all the groupoids π1 M_{g,I}, functorially in I (for g fixed) along monomorphisms I' ↪ I via the forgetful maps.
(ii) For each MD-graph G, determine the extension S π1 M_G of π1 M_G ≅ ∏_α π1 M_{g_α, Î_α} by Z^{Ã(G)}. In modern language this is the fundamental group of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of the boundary stratum, i.e. the stabiliser of a multicurve in the mapping class group, an extension of the product of the mapping class groups of the pieces by the free abelian group of Dehn twists along the edges.
(iii) For each generalisation morphism G → G' (edge contraction / specialisation, including isomorphisms), determine the induced groupoid maps S π1 M_G → S π1 M_{G'}.

The whole programme is a combinatorial, algebraic presentation of the 'Teichmüller tower' together with its tangential base points at infinity. This is the programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme. The next page turns to the relation between generalisation morphisms and 'multiplication' morphisms, looking at the effect at infinity of the forgetful maps.
errors: π1 M_G ≅ ∏ π1 M_{g_α, Î_α} holds only for the normalised/rigidified stratum (graph with its edges and vertices labelled). For the actual stratum one must quotient by Aut(G), and the Z^{edges} part is then not central. Grothendieck implicitly works with the rigidified version, which is fine, but the identification is not literally true for the stratum in M̄_{g,ν}.
Calling forgetful maps 'morphismes de normalisation' is idiosyncratic terminology, not an error. The maps π1 M_{g,I} → π1 M_{g,I'} require stability (2g−2+|I'|>0), which is not stated here.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a fully algebraic description (by generators and relations) of the whole diagram of local fundamental groups at infinity S π1 M_G, indexed by stable graphs with specialisation maps along edge contractions. This is a stratified 'π1 at infinity' system, more than the Teichmüller tower itself. Partial realisations exist (Lego–Teichmüller, profinite work of Boggi and Hoshi–Mochizuki), but a systematic presentation of this graph-indexed diagram as one algebraic object seems not to have been written down in exactly this form.
missed.quote: pour [un] MD-graphe G, déterminer l'extension Sπ1 M_G de π1 M_G ≃ ∏ π1 M_{g_α,Î_α} par Z^{Ã(G)}, et pour un morphisme de généralisation G → G' ... déterminer les morphismes de groupoïdes de généralisation correspondants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such a diagram is the natural input for a GT-action at all boundary strata and for anabelian reconstruction of the boundary. It documents that Grothendieck planned the stratified version explicitly, which is relevant to the history of Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The programme matches what Esquisse d'un programme announces (the Teichmüller tower by generators and relations, structure at infinity). The extension by Dehn twists is classical, as multicurve stabilisers. The explicit stratified formulation is a nice unpublished detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The displayed formula is most likely 𝔖_{I,I'} ≃ 𝔖_{I'} × 𝔖_{I∖I'}: the stabiliser of I' in the symmetric group, written with a script S/𝔖. It is not a graph G.
'entre multiples associés aux graphes MD-pointés' is probably 'entre multiplicités [modulaires] associées aux graphes ...'.
The interlinear insertion reads roughly 'pour pouvoir visualiser bel et bien l'interaction des π1 M des [morphismes de normalisation]'. The current transcription garbles it.
